subject: DPA: incident notification timelines & subprocessor cooperation
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex.park@finrise.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: security@finrise.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: incident notification — proposed language

Jasmine — thanks for picking this up. Attached is our redline of the DPA section on incident notification. A few items where we need clarity from Redwood before legal can sign off: 

- Timeline: your current draft is 'without undue delay' + '30 days for final report'. We need an explicit initial notice SLA (we're proposing 48 hours for incidents impacting customer data).
- Scope: confirm whether incidents at subprocessors that could affect Finrise customers are treated the same as Redwood incidents.
- Evidence & cooperation: we expect timely access to audit logs and forensic findings. Please confirm typical handover windows and any constraints (e.g., log retention, export formats).
- Cross‑border: if incidents trigger notification to EU supervisory authorities, how will Redwood coordinate with Finrise on regulator communications and timeline?

We attached a redline with inline comments. Can your team respond with a proposed clause and acceptable timelines by EOD Friday?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Park | Head of Security, Finrise

Attachment: Finrise-DPA-redline-v3.docx (docx)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@finrise.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notification — proposed language

Alex — appreciate the clear redline. Looping in Marissa (ops), Ben (security), and Kim (legal) to align. High level position from our side below; I'll follow with a short proposed clause.

- Initial notice: Redwood can commit to an initial customer notification within 48 hours of detection for incidents that materially affect the customer's data or availability. The notice will include a summary of scope, affected customers (if identifiable), and immediate mitigations.
- Follow-up report: Updated findings and remediation plan within 5 business days, with a more detailed final report within 30 calendar days or sooner where practicable.
- Subprocessors: Redwood requires subprocessors to notify Redwood within 24 hours of detection of incidents that may affect Redwood customer data. Redwood will then evaluate and notify impacted customers under the same 48-hour initial-notice SLA.
- Evidence/cooperation: Redwood will provide audit logs, metadata, and core forensic findings within 7 business days where available. Full forensic exports (disk images, raw memory) will be provided only when legally required or on a case-by-case basis with appropriate NDAs and reasonable cost-recovery for third-party forensic work.
- Cross-border/regulator coordination: For incidents triggering EU supervisory authority notification, Redwood will provide the technical facts and timeline to Finrise as soon as they are available and will coordinate statements where joint communications make sense. Redwood reserves the right to comply with local retention or disclosure laws that limit what can be shared.

We're drafting a short clause that captures the above and will attach draft language in a follow-up e-mail. If any of that is a hard blocker for Finrise, please flag specific items so we can discuss exceptions.

Jasmine Liu
Security & Privacy Program Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notification — proposed language

Adding a few operational constraints from the security/ops side: 

- Forensic access: we should avoid automatic entitlement to raw host/DISK images. Offer a tiered access model: (1) audit logs and application-level traces (T+7 business days), (2) sanitized forensic reports (T+10 business days), (3) raw artifacts only on legal compulsion or signed SOW for forensic engagement.
- Log retention/export: clarify retention windows per log type; if Finrise needs longer retention, we can discuss retention add-ons.
- Subprocessor SLA: 24 hours to notify Redwood is aggressive but doable for major cloud providers; for downstream partners (managed services), we should qualify 'notify' as 'initial report' with follow-up within 72 hours.
- Cost & scope: extended forensic work beyond provisioned incident support should be billable or done under an SOW — add a line on 'reasonable cost recovery'.

I'll draft sample clause language for the forensic access section and attach the incident-evidence-template.xlsx so we have a mutual format for exchanged artifacts.

Ben
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: incident notification — proposed language

Legal notes: 

- GDPR supervisory authority notification: remember the 72-hour window to notify the supervisory authority where feasible (Art. 33). Our customer-facing time commitments (48 hours initial notice) are compatible, but we need to make the clause clear that Redwood will cooperate with Finrise on regulatory reporting; final decisions on regulatory filings should be done jointly.
- Definition: we must include a precise definition of 'Security Incident' / 'Personal Data Breach' (reference Art. 4(12) GDPR) to avoid ambiguity.
- Privilege & law enforcement: investigations involving law enforcement or internal privileged analysis may limit what we can share; we need carveouts and a statement about lawful restrictions.
- Cross-border transfers: if Finrise requires onward transfers to jurisdictions with additional controls, include a clause that the parties will update the DPA and perform any necessary transfer impact assessments or adopt SCCs as needed.

I'll notate the clause draft with guarded language and propose a mutual timeline table.

Kim
General Counsel (Privacy) | Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>

Alex — attached is our proposed clause (redline) and the incident evidence template. Key points in the draft: 

1) Definitions: 'Security Incident' and 'Personal Data Breach' defined consistent with GDPR.
2) Initial notice: Redwood to provide initial notification to customer within 48 hours of detection for incidents materially affecting the customer's data.
3) Follow-up and final report: preliminary findings within 5 business days; final report within 30 calendar days (with an option to extend for legitimate investigatory reasons).
4) Subprocessor incidents: subprocessors required to report to Redwood within 24 hours onboarding; Redwood to evaluate and notify impacted customers under the 48-hour window. For downstream partners we qualify the initial report window to 72 hours.
5) Evidence & forensic cooperation: audit logs and high-level forensic reports provided within 7 business days. Raw artifacts provided only on legal compulsion or a separately executed SOW. Reasonable cost recovery permitted.
6) Regulatory coordination: Redwood will cooperate with customer on supervisory authority notifications and provide technical information to assist Finrise with filings.

Please review the attached redline and the evidence template and send any comments by Friday 07 May so legal teams can exchange an agreed draft next week.

Thanks,
Jasmine

Jasmine / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clarity. A few responses from Finrise legal/security based on your draft: 

- Initial notice SLA: we can accept 48 hours for initial notice.
- Evidence handover: Finrise prefers a 7-calendar-day window for initial evidence (logs & reports). That aligns with Redwood's proposal.
- Subprocessor timing: we pushed for 12 hours to Redwood; given operations constraints we can accept Redwood's 24-hour requirement provided Redwood confirms escalation to customers within the same 48-hour SLA upon validation.
- Raw artifacts: Finrise accepts the 'legal compulsion or SOW' condition. We will flag scenarios where expedited raw artifact transfer is critical for regulator engagement.
- EU regulator coordination: please confirm Redwood's process for jointly drafting regulator filings. We expect Redwood to supply technical statements within 72 hours of request to allow us to meet Art. 33 timelines.

We're attaching a short redline for the regulatory coordination section. If you can confirm the 72-hour technical statement turnaround for regulator support, we can move to legal redline exchange next week.

Emily Zhou
Senior Counsel, Finrise
